At the edge of town, there was a bench with a crooked leg. Nobody knew who had put it there, facing a field that grew nothing but tall grass and the occasional stubborn sunflower.

People sat on it anyway. A bus driver ate her lunch there every Thursday. Two brothers used it as a finish line for their races. An old man came at dusk and watched the light leave the field, slowly enough that it never seemed to go.

One spring morning, someone wedged a flat stone beneath the crooked leg. The bench stopped rocking. No note was left; no one claimed the repair.

By summer, the stone had settled into the dirt, and grass had grown around it. The bench looked as though it had always stood steady.
